newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit steady after early rise vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit steady after early rise vs dollar.

text.p: The ringgit stuck to a steady path for most of the session, after an early jump due to dollar sales by offshore banks, dealers said.
"We didn't do much after the dollar/ringgit fall due to selling by Singapore" banks, said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Some dealers said the early market movements were boosted by ringgit buying from Kuala Lumpur-based corporates and not by the offshore parties.
"The power players came in and we just followed the trend," said another dealer.
The Malaysian currency was earlier predicted to trade in a tight range above 2.48 dollar.
Dealers remained unanimous that the ringgit's upward momentum against the dollar was intact, helped by its firmness against the lower-yielding Singapore dollar.
At the 1000 GMT Kuala Lumpur closing, ringgit was at 2.4771/78 a dollar from 2.4802/12 at its Friday local close.
The Singapore dollar was at 1.7275/92 ringgit from 1.7293/12 previously.
